issues.description: The console log warns 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative, fixed, or absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly.' This indicates a scroll-offset library (likely react-scroll or similar) has a container without a positioned ancestor.
issues.root_cause: A component on this page uses a scroll-offset hook or library and its container element is missing a CSS position property (relative/fixed/absolute). The wrapper div likely has default static positioning.

issues.description: page:mount event fires twice in the console logs (duplicate entries at nearly identical timestamps). Suggests the component or its parent is mounting twice, likely due to React StrictMode double-invoking effects in development.
issues.element: Step-1 page component useEffect / event emitter
issues.root_cause: React StrictMode in development intentionally double-invokes effects. The page:mount event is being logged inside a useEffect without a guard, causing two identical events. This is dev-only behavior and does not affect production, but could skew analytics.

fixes.reason: Adding 'relative' positioning to the outermost container div resolves the scroll-offset warning by ensuring the container has a non-static position for any scroll-offset calculations.
Guarding the logEvent call with a local flag prevents duplicate mount events from being fired during React StrictMode's double-invocation of effects in development.
